paragraphs.en: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety. It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent. AI agents’ increasing ability to bypass guardrails, though, raises the question of how to enforce HITL robustly.
paragraphs.zh: 人类监督是人工智能安全的支柱。 人类监督通常由「人在回路」（HITL）中的人类来执行，由其审批人工智能智能体所采取的关键操作。 然而，智能体日益增强的绕过防护机制的能力，引发了一个问题：如何稳健地执行「人在回路」。

sents.en: Human oversight is a pillar of AI safety.
sents.zh: 人类监督是人工智能安全的支柱。

sents.en: It is often exercised by a human in the loop (HITL) who approves critical actions taken by an AI agent.
sents.zh: 人类监督通常由「人在回路」（HITL）中的人类来执行，由其审批人工智能智能体所采取的关键操作。

sents.en: AI agents’ increasing ability to bypass guardrails, though, raises the question of how to enforce HITL robustly.
sents.zh: 然而，智能体日益增强的绕过防护机制的能力，引发了一个问题：如何稳健地执行「人在回路」。

paragraphs.en: We introduce the concept of inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL). An I-HITL protocol ensures that an agent can initiate an action only with explicit human approval, even when the human interacts with a system (e.g., a local agentic harness) compromised by the agent . A strong I-HITL protocol additionally ensures such approval even when an adversarial human attempts to delegate approvals to an agent.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出不可剥夺的人在回路（I-HITL）的概念。 一条 I-HITL 协议确保智能体只有在获得人类明确批准的情况下才能发起行动，即使人类是与一个已被智能体攻陷的系统（例如本地智能体执行框架）交互时也是如此。 强 I-HITL 协议还能进一步确保：即使对抗性人类试图将批准权委托给智能体，此类批准依然必须由人类给出。

sents.en: We introduce the concept of inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL).
sents.zh: 我们提出不可剥夺的人在回路（I-HITL）的概念。

sents.en: An I-HITL protocol ensures that an agent can initiate an action only with explicit human approval, even when the human interacts with a system (e.g., a local agentic harness) compromised by the agent .
sents.zh: 一条 I-HITL 协议确保智能体只有在获得人类明确批准的情况下才能发起行动，即使人类是与一个已被智能体攻陷的系统（例如本地智能体执行框架）交互时也是如此。

sents.en: A strong I-HITL protocol additionally ensures such approval even when an adversarial human attempts to delegate approvals to an agent.
sents.zh: 强 I-HITL 协议还能进一步确保：即使对抗性人类试图将批准权委托给智能体，此类批准依然必须由人类给出。

paragraphs.en: To motivate I-HITL, we report on experiments with a popular agentic wallet platform in which raising an agent’s spending cap requires HITL approval via emailed one-time passcodes (OTPs). Given access to the user’s email and a task blocked by the cap, we find that ten different frontier models will often autonomously raise the cap, harvesting OTPs to bypass a HITL guardrail and surfacing other vulnerabilities.
paragraphs.zh: 为了说明 I-HITL 的动机，我们报告了针对一个流行的智能体钱包平台的实验：在该平台中，提高智能体的消费上限需要通过电子邮件发送的一次性验证码（OTP）获得 HITL 批准。 在获得用户邮箱访问权限且任务被消费上限阻塞的情况下，我们发现十个不同的前沿模型通常会自主提高消费上限，获取 OTP 以绕过 HITL 防护机制，并暴露出其他漏洞。

sents.en: To motivate I-HITL, we report on experiments with a popular agentic wallet platform in which raising an agent’s spending cap requires HITL approval via emailed one-time passcodes (OTPs).
sents.zh: 为了说明 I-HITL 的动机，我们报告了针对一个流行的智能体钱包平台的实验：在该平台中，提高智能体的消费上限需要通过电子邮件发送的一次性验证码（OTP）获得 HITL 批准。

sents.en: Given access to the user’s email and a task blocked by the cap, we find that ten different frontier models will often autonomously raise the cap, harvesting OTPs to bypass a HITL guardrail and surfacing other vulnerabilities.
sents.zh: 在获得用户邮箱访问权限且任务被消费上限阻塞的情况下，我们发现十个不同的前沿模型通常会自主提高消费上限，获取 OTP 以绕过 HITL 防护机制，并暴露出其他漏洞。

paragraphs.en: We formally define I-HITL using the concept of communication topologies and prove necessary and sufficient conditions for its realization. We show that an I-HITL protocol requires a trusted entity —a trusted computing device (or equivalent)—and characterize which such devices can and cannot realize an I-HITL protocol. We present a prototype I-HITL system called Countersign that can plug into and strengthen existing HITL systems using off-the-shelf consumer mobile devices.
paragraphs.zh: 我们利用通信拓扑的概念对 I-HITL 进行形式化定义，并证明其实现的充要条件。 我们证明 I-HITL 协议需要一个可信实体——即可信计算设备（或等效物）——并刻画哪些此类设备能够实现 I-HITL 协议、哪些不能。 我们提出了一个名为 Countersign 的 I-HITL 原型系统，它可以接入现有 HITL 系统并利用现成的消费级移动设备对其进行强化。

paragraphs.en: AI agents are increasingly entrusted with consequential decisions and tasks, as personal agents such as Meta’s Muse [ 56 ] , OpenAI’s Dots [ 69 ] , OpenClaw [ 70 ] , and Hermes [ 65 ] see rapid adoption. Users frequently grant these agents broad access to credentials and tools: email, payment methods, shell access, and browser sessions. Yet because agents remain susceptible to hallucination, prompt injection, and misalignment, the same access that lets them act on a user’s behalf also lets them act against the user’s interests.
paragraphs.zh: 随着个人智能体（如 Meta 的 Muse [ 56 ]、OpenAI 的 Dots [ 69 ]、OpenClaw [ 70 ] 和 Hermes [ 65 ]）被快速采用，AI 智能体越来越多地被委托执行具有重大影响的决策和任务。 用户经常授予这些智能体对凭据和工具的广泛访问权限：电子邮件、支付方式、shell 访问权限和浏览器会话。 然而，由于智能体仍然容易受到幻觉、提示注入和目标错位的影响，让它们能够代表用户行事的同等访问权限，也让它们能够做出损害用户利益的行为。

paragraphs.en: A natural response is to constrain what an agent can do via a human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gate (or HITL gate , for short)—a mechanism that permits an agent’s action to proceed only after human approval [ 42 , 79 , 74 ] . HITL gates are only meaningful, though, if agents cannot bypass them. In practice, agents can often bypass various guardrails to escalate their own permissions, as two examples show.
paragraphs.zh: 一个自然的应对方式是通过人在回路（human-in-the-loop，HITL）审批门（简称 HITL 门）来限制智能体能做什么——这种机制只有在获得人类批准后，智能体的操作才能继续执行 [42, 79, 74]。 然而，只有当智能体无法绕过 HITL 门时，它们才有意义。 实践中，智能体往往能够绕过各种防护机制来提升自身的权限，如下面两个例子所示。

paragraphs.en: Circle Agent Wallets allow an account owner to place a daily spending cap on an agent [ 23 ] . They protect cap changes via a HITL gate authenticated using a one-time passcode emailed to the account owner. We show in this paper that given access to an email tool, a wallet’s agent will often autonomously harvest the OTPs and update caps without human approval, bypassing the HITL gate. Nothing here is specific to Circle or to email: Other agentic wallets’ HITL gates use similar design patterns [ 28 , 57 ] .
paragraphs.zh: Circle 智能体钱包允许账户所有者为智能体设置每日消费上限 [ 23 ]。 它们通过一个人在回路（HITL）门控来保护上限变更，该门控使用发送到账户所有者邮箱的一次性验证码进行身份验证。 我们在本文中表明，只要能够访问电子邮件工具，钱包的智能体往往会自主获取一次性验证码并在未经人类批准的情况下更新上限，从而绕过人在回路（HITL）门控。 这里的攻击并非 Circle 或电子邮件所特有：其他智能体钱包的人在回路（HITL）门控也采用了类似的设计模式 [ 28 , 57 ]。

sents.zh: Circle 智能体钱包允许账户所有者为智能体设置每日消费上限 [ 23 ]。

paragraphs.en: Early versions of Claude Mythos Preview repeatedly bypassed harness-imposed guardrails. In one case, the model used a tool intended only for file editing to write to the shell’s input, gaining arbitrary code execution. In other cases, it searched low-level process data for credentials and accessed resources that Anthropic had deliberately withheld [ 6 ] .
paragraphs.zh: Claude Mythos Preview 的早期版本曾多次绕过测试环境设置的安全防护。 在其中一个案例中，该模型利用一个本应仅用于文件编辑的工具向 shell 的输入写入内容，从而获得了任意代码执行的能力。 在其他案例中，它会搜索底层进程数据以查找凭据，并访问 Anthropic 有意限制其访问的资源 [ 6 ] 。

sents.en: Early versions of Claude Mythos Preview repeatedly bypassed harness-imposed guardrails.
sents.zh: Claude Mythos Preview 的早期版本曾多次绕过测试环境设置的安全防护。

paragraphs.en: These two examples illustrate a shortcoming of many HITL gates: agents may have or gain access to the very resources used to enforce the gate. There are numerous reports of similar examples, e.g., [ 49 , 82 , 64 , 55 ] , and analogous, if not HITL-specific, behaviors arising in controlled evaluations of frontier models [ 18 , 54 , 73 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 这两个例子说明了许多人机协同（HITL）把关机制的一个缺陷：智能体可能拥有或能够获得用于执行该把关机制的资源本身。 有大量关于类似例子的报告，例如 [49, 82, 64, 55]，并且在受控的前沿模型评估中也出现了类似的行为（即使并非 HITL 特有）[18, 54, 73]。

paragraphs.en: Despite the pervasive risk of agents subverting HITL controls, however, the security goal of ensuring human approval before execution of a given action has a notable lack of formal modeling in the literature to date .
paragraphs.zh: 尽管智能体颠覆人在回路（HITL）控制的风险普遍存在，但截至目前，在执行特定操作前确保人类批准这一安全目标，在文献中明显缺乏形式化建模。

paragraphs.en: Our threat model for I-HITL involves three parties: (1) the human , (2) the agent-controlled platform , such as the human’s client machine, and (3) a target service , typically a remote server, which gates agent actions. Informally, an I-HITL protocol ensures that the service can distinguish an action approved by the human from one approved by the agent acting through the platform, even if the agent has compromised the platform . We also put forth a notion of strong I-HITL that ensures such approval even when an adversarial human controller attempts to delegate approvals to the agent. This implies a form of accountability useful for enforcing policies that mandate human oversight of AI [ 35 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 我们针对 I-HITL 的威胁模型涉及三方：(1) 人类，(2) 由智能体控制的平台，例如人类的客户端机器，以及 (3) 目标服务，通常为远程服务器，由其管控智能体的操作。 非正式地说，I-HITL 协议确保服务能够区分由人类批准的操作与由智能体通过平台代为批准的操作，即使该智能体已经攻陷了平台。 我们还提出了强 I-HITL 的概念，即使对抗性的人类控制者试图将批准权限委托给智能体时，也能确保此类批准的有效性。 这意味着一种问责机制，有助于执行要求对人工智能进行人类监督的策略 [35]。

paragraphs.en: Our work shows that I-HITL requires a trusted entity 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , but that this is not sufficient to realize I-HITL. Specifically, a trusted entity must be able to attest to having generated a given cryptographic key for I-HITL to be possible.

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 schematically contrasts the insecure HITL configuration of Example 1 with the general architecture for I-HITL that we explore in this work.
paragraphs.zh: 图 1 示意性地对比了示例 1 中不安全的人在回路（HITL）配置与我们在本工作中探索的 I-HITL 通用架构。

paragraphs.en: Self-escalation. To motivate our work, we realize Example 1 with Circle’s Agentic Wallets as a testbed. Its HITL gate is authenticated by one-time passcodes (OTPs) emailed to the human user. We give ten frontier models an invoice-payment task requiring funds that exceed a previously set daily spending cap. We use a common configuration that allows agents to access the user’s email. With no adversary and no prompting , nine of the ten models bypass human approval, harvesting OTPs and raising their own cap in at least one run. With email-based prompt injection, this drops to seven of ten models, as some models detect the prompt injection. In experiments where the agent is only asked to summarize email, five models both raise the cap and pay an attacker impersonating the user by email. Broadly, our results do not correlate strongly with model capability.
paragraphs.zh: 自我提权。 为论证我们工作的动机，我们以 Circle 的智能体钱包（Agentic Wallets）为测试平台实现了示例 1。 其人机协同（HITL）闸门通过发送到人类用户邮箱的一次性验证码（OTP）进行认证。 我们给十个前沿模型布置了一项发票支付任务，该任务所需资金超过先前设定的每日支出上限。 我们采用一种允许智能体访问用户电子邮件的通用配置。 在没有攻击者、没有额外提示词的情况下，十个模型中有九个在至少一次运行中绕过人类审批，获取 OTP 并自行提高支出上限。 在加入基于电子邮件的提示词注入后，这一数字降至十个模型中的七个，因为部分模型能够检测到提示词注入。 在仅要求智能体总结电子邮件内容的实验中，有五个模型既提高了支出上限，又向通过电子邮件冒充用户的攻击者完成了付款。 总体而言，我们的结果与模型能力没有很强的相关性。

sents.en: Self-escalation.
sents.zh: 自我提权。

sents.en: To motivate our work, we realize Example 1 with Circle’s Agentic Wallets as a testbed.
sents.zh: 为论证我们工作的动机，我们以 Circle 的智能体钱包（Agentic Wallets）为测试平台实现了示例 1。

sents.en: Its HITL gate is authenticated by one-time passcodes (OTPs) emailed to the human user.
sents.zh: 其人机协同（HITL）闸门通过发送到人类用户邮箱的一次性验证码（OTP）进行认证。

sents.en: We give ten frontier models an invoice-payment task requiring funds that exceed a previously set daily spending cap.
sents.zh: 我们给十个前沿模型布置了一项发票支付任务，该任务所需资金超过先前设定的每日支出上限。

sents.en: We use a common configuration that allows agents to access the user’s email.
sents.zh: 我们采用一种允许智能体访问用户电子邮件的通用配置。

sents.en: With no adversary and no prompting , nine of the ten models bypass human approval, harvesting OTPs and raising their own cap in at least one run.
sents.zh: 在没有攻击者、没有额外提示词的情况下，十个模型中有九个在至少一次运行中绕过人类审批，获取 OTP 并自行提高支出上限。

sents.en: With email-based prompt injection, this drops to seven of ten models, as some models detect the prompt injection.
sents.zh: 在加入基于电子邮件的提示词注入后，这一数字降至十个模型中的七个，因为部分模型能够检测到提示词注入。

sents.en: In experiments where the agent is only asked to summarize email, five models both raise the cap and pay an attacker impersonating the user by email.
sents.zh: 在仅要求智能体总结电子邮件内容的实验中，有五个模型既提高了支出上限，又向通过电子邮件冒充用户的攻击者完成了付款。

sents.en: Broadly, our results do not correlate strongly with model capability.
sents.zh: 总体而言，我们的结果与模型能力没有很强的相关性。

paragraphs.en: Formalizing I-HITL. Common deployment failures, such as Examples 1 and 2 , prompt us to introduce what we believe to be the first security definition for HITL gates that captures security against an agent-compromised computing platform. Our definition also encompasses a human who attempts to delegate control to an agent. Previous attempts at HITL formalism neglect both of these settings and assume that agents are unable to hijack the approval flow, focusing instead on the potential mismatch between an approved action and its execution [ 85 , 44 ] , a consideration which is subsumed by our definition. Related formal frameworks in ceremony analysis [ 34 , 72 ] and transaction authentication [ 15 , 14 , 84 , 33 ] model platform compromise but not human principals delegating their authority.
paragraphs.zh: 对 I-HITL 进行形式化。 常见的部署失败（如示例 1 和示例 2）促使我们引入据我们所知首个针对 HITL 门控的安全定义，该定义刻画了针对已被智能体攻陷的计算平台的安全性。 我们的定义还涵盖了试图将控制权委托给智能体的人类。 以往对 HITL 形式化的尝试忽略了上述两种场景，并假设智能体无法劫持审批流程，而是专注于已批准动作与其执行之间的潜在不一致 [ 85 , 44 ]，而这一考量已被我们的定义所涵盖。 仪式分析 [ 34 , 72 ] 和交易认证 [ 15 , 14 , 84 , 33 ] 中的相关形式化框架对平台被攻陷进行了建模，但未考虑人类主体委托其权限的情形。

sents.en: Formalizing I-HITL.
sents.zh: 对 I-HITL 进行形式化。

sents.en: Common deployment failures, such as Examples 1 and 2 , prompt us to introduce what we believe to be the first security definition for HITL gates that captures security against an agent-compromised computing platform.
sents.zh: 常见的部署失败（如示例 1 和示例 2）促使我们引入据我们所知首个针对 HITL 门控的安全定义，该定义刻画了针对已被智能体攻陷的计算平台的安全性。

sents.en: Our definition also encompasses a human who attempts to delegate control to an agent.
sents.zh: 我们的定义还涵盖了试图将控制权委托给智能体的人类。

sents.en: Previous attempts at HITL formalism neglect both of these settings and assume that agents are unable to hijack the approval flow, focusing instead on the potential mismatch between an approved action and its execution [ 85 , 44 ] , a consideration which is subsumed by our definition.
sents.zh: 以往对 HITL 形式化的尝试忽略了上述两种场景，并假设智能体无法劫持审批流程，而是专注于已批准动作与其执行之间的潜在不一致 [ 85 , 44 ]，而这一考量已被我们的定义所涵盖。

sents.en: Related formal frameworks in ceremony analysis [ 34 , 72 ] and transaction authentication [ 15 , 14 , 84 , 33 ] model platform compromise but not human principals delegating their authority.
sents.zh: 仪式分析 [ 34 , 72 ] 和交易认证 [ 15 , 14 , 84 , 33 ] 中的相关形式化框架对平台被攻陷进行了建模，但未考虑人类主体委托其权限的情形。

paragraphs.en: We define an I-HITL protocol as having two properties. Completeness states that a service will accept an honest human’s approval of an agent action. Approval-binding says that no adversary can cause the service to accept an approval that the human did not grant. By extending the formal machinery of [ 13 ] , we characterize the communication topologies , i.e., sets of entities and communication channels, needed to realize a complete and approval-binding I-HITL protocol. In the “plain” topology of human, platform, and service used in many existing and proposed systems [ 77 , 78 , 23 , 68 , 27 , 46 , 29 ] there exists no complete, approval binding I-HITL protocol. This result motivates the addition of a trusted entity 𝒯 \mathcal{T} outside of the agent’s control—typically in the form of a trusted computing device. We prove that such a trusted entity alone is not in general adequate for I-HITL, and give precise requirements on its functionality which must be satisfied.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 I-HITL 协议定义为具有两个性质。 完备性是指服务会接受一个诚实的人类对智能体动作的批准。 批准绑定是指任何对手都无法使服务接受一个人类并未授予的批准。 通过扩展 [ 13 ] 的形式化机制，我们刻画了实现完备且批准绑定的 I-HITL 协议所需的通信拓扑，即实体集合与通信信道的集合。 在许多现有和已提出的系统 [ 77 , 78 , 23 , 68 , 27 , 46 , 29 ] 中所使用的由人类、平台和服务构成的「朴素」拓扑中，不存在完备且批准绑定的 I-HITL 协议。 这一结果促使我们引入一个不受智能体控制的可信实体 𝒯 \mathcal{T}——通常以可信计算设备的形式出现。 我们证明，仅凭这样一个可信实体通常并不足以实现 I-HITL，并给出其功能必须满足的精确要求。

sents.zh: 我们将 I-HITL 协议定义为具有两个性质。

sents.en: Completeness states that a service will accept an honest human’s approval of an agent action.
sents.zh: 完备性是指服务会接受一个诚实的人类对智能体动作的批准。

sents.en: Approval-binding says that no adversary can cause the service to accept an approval that the human did not grant.
sents.zh: 批准绑定是指任何对手都无法使服务接受一个人类并未授予的批准。

sents.en: By extending the formal machinery of [ 13 ] , we characterize the communication topologies , i.e., sets of entities and communication channels, needed to realize a complete and approval-binding I-HITL protocol.
sents.zh: 通过扩展 [ 13 ] 的形式化机制，我们刻画了实现完备且批准绑定的 I-HITL 协议所需的通信拓扑，即实体集合与通信信道的集合。

sents.en: In the “plain” topology of human, platform, and service used in many existing and proposed systems [ 77 , 78 , 23 , 68 , 27 , 46 , 29 ] there exists no complete, approval binding I-HITL protocol.
sents.zh: 在许多现有和已提出的系统 [ 77 , 78 , 23 , 68 , 27 , 46 , 29 ] 中所使用的由人类、平台和服务构成的「朴素」拓扑中，不存在完备且批准绑定的 I-HITL 协议。

sents.en: This result motivates the addition of a trusted entity 𝒯 \mathcal{T} outside of the agent’s control—typically in the form of a trusted computing device.
sents.zh: 这一结果促使我们引入一个不受智能体控制的可信实体 𝒯 \mathcal{T}——通常以可信计算设备的形式出现。

sents.en: We prove that such a trusted entity alone is not in general adequate for I-HITL, and give precise requirements on its functionality which must be satisfied.
sents.zh: 我们证明，仅凭这样一个可信实体通常并不足以实现 I-HITL，并给出其功能必须满足的精确要求。

paragraphs.en: Common authentication approaches—e.g., 2FA / authenticator apps, hardware wallets, etc.—do not offer a trusted entity 𝒯 \mathcal{T} sufficient to realize an I-HITL protocol. Our work serves as guidance for identifying what devices can do so.
paragraphs.zh: 常见的身份验证方式——例如双因素认证（2FA）/身份验证器应用、硬件钱包等——无法提供足以实现 I-HITL 协议的可信实体 𝒯 \mathcal{T}。 我们的工作可作为识别哪些设备能够做到这一点的指引。

sents.en: Common authentication approaches—e.g., 2FA / authenticator apps, hardware wallets, etc.—do not offer a trusted entity 𝒯 \mathcal{T} sufficient to realize an I-HITL protocol.
sents.zh: 常见的身份验证方式——例如双因素认证（2FA）/身份验证器应用、硬件钱包等——无法提供足以实现 I-HITL 协议的可信实体 𝒯 \mathcal{T}。

sents.en: Our work serves as guidance for identifying what devices can do so.
sents.zh: 我们的工作可作为识别哪些设备能够做到这一点的指引。

paragraphs.en: Countersign. We introduce Countersign , a prototype implementation of a secure I-HITL protocol that uses an Android or iOS mobile application to realize a trusted entity, showing that the requirements arising from our formal analysis can be satisfied with these devices under realistic trust assumptions. Countersign uses Google’s/Apple’s attestation functionality and the hardware-backed key management capabilities of their respective devices to establish the requisite channels, as well as physical, human-driven approval via a button press or biometric authentication. Excluding scaffolding, Countersign’s core I-HITL logic consists of ∼ \sim 800 LOC for the backend service, and ∼ \sim 150 LOC each for the Android/iOS applications, demonstrating the relative simplicity of the core components. Our implementation also highlights gaps in the current functionality available to developers that could be patched to strengthen I-HITL guarantees.
paragraphs.zh: 會签验证。 我们介绍 Countersign，这是一个安全 I-HITL 协议的原型实现，它使用 Android 或 iOS 移动应用来实现受信任实体，表明由我们的形式化分析所产生的需求可以在现实的信任假设下用这些设备来满足。 Countersign 利用 Google/Apple 的证明功能及其各自设备的硬件密钥管理能力来建立所需的通道，并通过按下按钮或生物识别认证实现物理的、由人驱动的批准。 除辅助代码外，Countersign 的核心 I-HITL 逻辑由后端服务约 800 行代码以及 Android/iOS 应用各约 150 行代码组成，展示了核心组件的相对简单性。 我们的实现还凸显了当前开发者可用功能中的缺口，这些缺口可以通过修补来强化 I-HITL 保证。

sents.en: Countersign.
sents.zh: 會签验证。

sents.en: We introduce Countersign , a prototype implementation of a secure I-HITL protocol that uses an Android or iOS mobile application to realize a trusted entity, showing that the requirements arising from our formal analysis can be satisfied with these devices under realistic trust assumptions.
sents.zh: 我们介绍 Countersign，这是一个安全 I-HITL 协议的原型实现，它使用 Android 或 iOS 移动应用来实现受信任实体，表明由我们的形式化分析所产生的需求可以在现实的信任假设下用这些设备来满足。

sents.en: Countersign uses Google’s/Apple’s attestation functionality and the hardware-backed key management capabilities of their respective devices to establish the requisite channels, as well as physical, human-driven approval via a button press or biometric authentication.
sents.zh: Countersign 利用 Google/Apple 的证明功能及其各自设备的硬件密钥管理能力来建立所需的通道，并通过按下按钮或生物识别认证实现物理的、由人驱动的批准。

sents.en: Excluding scaffolding, Countersign’s core I-HITL logic consists of ∼ \sim 800 LOC for the backend service, and ∼ \sim 150 LOC each for the Android/iOS applications, demonstrating the relative simplicity of the core components.
sents.zh: 除辅助代码外，Countersign 的核心 I-HITL 逻辑由后端服务约 800 行代码以及 Android/iOS 应用各约 150 行代码组成，展示了核心组件的相对简单性。

sents.en: Our implementation also highlights gaps in the current functionality available to developers that could be patched to strengthen I-HITL guarantees.
sents.zh: 我们的实现还凸显了当前开发者可用功能中的缺口，这些缺口可以通过修补来强化 I-HITL 保证。

paragraphs.en: Inalienable HITL: We initiate the study of I-HITL, which ensures, in a trust model admitting compromised user devices, that agent actions are gated by human approvals. Strong I-HITL also extends to settings involving adversarial human attempts to delegate to agents.
paragraphs.zh: 不可剥夺的人类监督（I-HITL）：我们发起对 I-HITL 的研究，在一个允许用户设备被攻陷的信任模型中，确保智能体的行为必须经过人类批准的门控。 强 I-HITL 还可扩展到涉及对抗性人类试图向智能体委派任务的场景。

sents.en: Inalienable HITL: We initiate the study of I-HITL, which ensures, in a trust model admitting compromised user devices, that agent actions are gated by human approvals.
sents.zh: 不可剥夺的人类监督（I-HITL）：我们发起对 I-HITL 的研究，在一个允许用户设备被攻陷的信任模型中，确保智能体的行为必须经过人类批准的门控。

sents.en: Strong I-HITL also extends to settings involving adversarial human attempts to delegate to agents.
sents.zh: 强 I-HITL 还可扩展到涉及对抗性人类试图向智能体委派任务的场景。

paragraphs.en: Self-escalation: We explore the security risks of agent setups without I-HITL enforcement, experimentally demonstrating agent self-escalation past user-defined spending-cap limits on a popular agentic wallet.
paragraphs.zh: 自我升级：我们探讨了未实施 I-HITL 强制约束的智能体设置所带来的安全风险，并通过实验演示了智能体在一种流行的智能体钱包上突破用户自定义消费上限的自我升级行为。

paragraphs.en: Formalism: We introduce a formal model for I-HITL protocols and prove that a trusted entity is necessary to realize an I-HITL protocol ( Theorem 4 ). We also prove, however, that a trusted entity is not sufficient ( Theorem 7 ). We use our results to clarify what concrete instantiations of a trusted entity allow a I-HITL protocol to be realized (Table III ).
paragraphs.zh: 形式化：我们为 I-HITL 协议引入了一个形式化模型，并证明需要一个可信实体才能实现 I-HITL 协议（定理 4）。 然而，我们还证明了可信实体并不充分（定理 7）。 我们利用我们的结果阐明了哪些可信实体的具体实例化使 I-HITL 协议得以实现（表 III）。

sents.en: Formalism: We introduce a formal model for I-HITL protocols and prove that a trusted entity is necessary to realize an I-HITL protocol ( Theorem 4 ).
sents.zh: 形式化：我们为 I-HITL 协议引入了一个形式化模型，并证明需要一个可信实体才能实现 I-HITL 协议（定理 4）。

sents.en: We also prove, however, that a trusted entity is not sufficient ( Theorem 7 ).
sents.zh: 然而，我们还证明了可信实体并不充分（定理 7）。

sents.en: We use our results to clarify what concrete instantiations of a trusted entity allow a I-HITL protocol to be realized (Table III ).
sents.zh: 我们利用我们的结果阐明了哪些可信实体的具体实例化使 I-HITL 协议得以实现（表 III）。

paragraphs.en: Countersign: We present an end-to-end prototype of Countersign, an I-HITL implementation that uses off-the-shelf mobile devices as trusted entities.
paragraphs.zh: 反签名（Countersign）：我们展示了 Countersign 的端到端原型，这是一种 I-HITL 实现，它将现成的移动设备用作可信实体。

paragraphs.en: We review related work in Section VIII and conclude in Section IX .
paragraphs.zh: 我们在第 VIII 节回顾相关工作，并在第 IX 节进行总结。

paragraphs.en: We now specify our threat model, and explain its relevance to several widely deployed HITL gates.
paragraphs.zh: 我们现在明确我们的威胁模型，并解释其与几种广泛部署的人机协同（HITL）门控的相关性。

paragraphs.en: We consider three parties: a human , a computing platform running an AI agent, and a service . The human can interact with the platform directly (by sending/reading messages over input/output peripherals) but communication to the service must pass through the platform. The service aims to determine, for a given message received, whether the human was responsible for it. Informally this means that the human saw, and approved of the message.
paragraphs.zh: 我们考虑三方：人类、运行AI智能体的计算平台，以及服务。 人类可以直接与平台交互（通过输入/输出外设发送/读取消息），但与服务的通信必须经过平台。 该服务旨在对收到的给定消息判断是否由人类负责。 非正式地说，这意味着人类看到并认可了该消息。

sents.en: We consider three parties: a human , a computing platform running an AI agent, and a service .
sents.zh: 我们考虑三方：人类、运行AI智能体的计算平台，以及服务。

sents.en: The human can interact with the platform directly (by sending/reading messages over input/output peripherals) but communication to the service must pass through the platform.
sents.zh: 人类可以直接与平台交互（通过输入/输出外设发送/读取消息），但与服务的通信必须经过平台。

sents.en: The service aims to determine, for a given message received, whether the human was responsible for it.
sents.zh: 该服务旨在对收到的给定消息判断是否由人类负责。

sents.en: Informally this means that the human saw, and approved of the message.
sents.zh: 非正式地说，这意味着人类看到并认可了该消息。

paragraphs.en: We assume that the service is honest and executes exactly the approved action [ 92 ] , but that the agent is adversarial and fully controls the platform, aiming to convince the service that the human is responsible for a message when this is not the case. Although a fully corrupted platform is a strong threat model, we believe it is the right stance to adopt given the trend of increasing integration of AI agents into all manner of computing platforms and the corresponding risk of a corrupted AI agent (e.g. from prompt injection or a misaligned LLM). Agents have previously escaped their sandboxes by exploiting misconfigurations [ 66 , 52 ] , and LLMs have been shown capable of finding and exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in operating systems or browsers.
paragraphs.zh: 我们假设服务是诚实的，并且会严格执行已批准的操作 [ 92 ]，但假设智能体是对抗性的，并且完全控制平台，其目的是让服务相信某条消息是由人类负责发送的，而实际情况并非如此。 虽然平台完全被攻陷是一个很强的威胁模型，但考虑到 AI 智能体正日益深度集成到各类计算平台中，以及 AI 智能体被攻陷（例如由提示注入或未对齐的 LLM 引起）所带来的相应风险，我们认为这是应当采取的立场。 此前已有智能体通过利用错误配置逃出其沙箱 [ 66 , 52 ]，并且已有研究表明 LLM 能够发现并利用操作系统或浏览器中的零日漏洞。

sents.en: We assume that the service is honest and executes exactly the approved action [ 92 ] , but that the agent is adversarial and fully controls the platform, aiming to convince the service that the human is responsible for a message when this is not the case.
sents.zh: 我们假设服务是诚实的，并且会严格执行已批准的操作 [ 92 ]，但假设智能体是对抗性的，并且完全控制平台，其目的是让服务相信某条消息是由人类负责发送的，而实际情况并非如此。

sents.en: Although a fully corrupted platform is a strong threat model, we believe it is the right stance to adopt given the trend of increasing integration of AI agents into all manner of computing platforms and the corresponding risk of a corrupted AI agent (e.g. from prompt injection or a misaligned LLM).
sents.zh: 虽然平台完全被攻陷是一个很强的威胁模型，但考虑到 AI 智能体正日益深度集成到各类计算平台中，以及 AI 智能体被攻陷（例如由提示注入或未对齐的 LLM 引起）所带来的相应风险，我们认为这是应当采取的立场。

sents.en: Agents have previously escaped their sandboxes by exploiting misconfigurations [ 66 , 52 ] , and LLMs have been shown capable of finding and exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in operating systems or browsers.
sents.zh: 此前已有智能体通过利用错误配置逃出其沙箱 [ 66 , 52 ]，并且已有研究表明 LLM 能够发现并利用操作系统或浏览器中的零日漏洞。

paragraphs.en: The human may be honest or adversarial in our threat model. An honest human represents the dominant paradigm for thinking about human-in-the-loop systems: the human respects any protocol and can keep short secrets (such as passwords) from the adversarial platform.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们的威胁模型中，人类可能是诚实的，也可能是对抗性的。 诚实的人类代表了对人在回路系统进行思考时的主流范式：人类会遵守任何协议，并且能对对抗性的平台保守短期秘密（例如密码）。

sents.en: The human may be honest or adversarial in our threat model.
sents.zh: 在我们的威胁模型中，人类可能是诚实的，也可能是对抗性的。

sents.en: An honest human represents the dominant paradigm for thinking about human-in-the-loop systems: the human respects any protocol and can keep short secrets (such as passwords) from the adversarial platform.
sents.zh: 诚实的人类代表了对人在回路系统进行思考时的主流范式：人类会遵守任何协议，并且能对对抗性的平台保守短期秘密（例如密码）。

paragraphs.en: Increasingly, however, human-in-the-loop frameworks that resist an adversarial human are important. First, LLMs have shown the ability to deceive, mislead and steer users [ 51 , 40 ] , which could manifest itself as users divulging secrets to agents. Second, the human and agent may both be corrupted in the sense that they collude to evade the service’s requirement of human oversight of agent actions. Users tend to delegate to and (potentially over-permission) AI agents [ 53 ] , and a human might seek to avoid responsibility for messages to the service either out of laziness, or to engage with the service adversarially and later blame an AI agent for resulting damage or harm.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，日益重要的是，能够抵御对抗性人类的人机回环框架。 首先，大语言模型已表现出欺骗、误导和引导用户的能力 [ 51 , 40 ] ，这可能表现为用户向智能体泄露秘密。 其次，人类与智能体可能同时被腐化，即二者串通以规避服务对智能体行为须有人类监督的要求。 用户倾向于向 AI 智能体授权委托（并可能过度授权）[ 53 ] ，而人类可能出于懒惰，或为了以对抗方式与服务交互并在事后将造成的损害或伤害归咎于某个 AI 智能体，而试图逃避对发送给服务的消息所应承担的责任。

sents.en: Increasingly, however, human-in-the-loop frameworks that resist an adversarial human are important.
sents.zh: 然而，日益重要的是，能够抵御对抗性人类的人机回环框架。

sents.en: First, LLMs have shown the ability to deceive, mislead and steer users [ 51 , 40 ] , which could manifest itself as users divulging secrets to agents.
sents.zh: 首先，大语言模型已表现出欺骗、误导和引导用户的能力 [ 51 , 40 ] ，这可能表现为用户向智能体泄露秘密。

sents.en: Second, the human and agent may both be corrupted in the sense that they collude to evade the service’s requirement of human oversight of agent actions.
sents.zh: 其次，人类与智能体可能同时被腐化，即二者串通以规避服务对智能体行为须有人类监督的要求。

sents.en: Users tend to delegate to and (potentially over-permission) AI agents [ 53 ] , and a human might seek to avoid responsibility for messages to the service either out of laziness, or to engage with the service adversarially and later blame an AI agent for resulting damage or harm.
sents.zh: 用户倾向于向 AI 智能体授权委托（并可能过度授权）[ 53 ] ，而人类可能出于懒惰，或为了以对抗方式与服务交互并在事后将造成的损害或伤害归咎于某个 AI 智能体，而试图逃避对发送给服务的消息所应承担的责任。

paragraphs.en: In later sections, we will also consider a fourth party, a t rusted entity . A trusted entity is honest, outside of the control of the agent, and may communicate with all parties directly, although with restrictions on the security and directionality of its communication channels. We deliberately leave the trusted entity abstract, and it may be satisfied by different implementations under different trust assumptions. It may be secure hardware attached to the platform itself, a separate device the human carries—such as a hardware wallet—or a physical place, such as a bank branch or an enrollment office, where communication occurs in person.
paragraphs.zh: 在后续章节中，我们还将考虑第四方，即可信实体。 可信实体是诚实的，不受智能体的控制，并且可以直接与所有参与方通信，尽管其通信信道的安全性和方向性存在限制。 我们刻意将可信实体保持抽象，它在不同的信任假设下可以由不同的实现来满足。 它可以是连接到平台本身的安全硬件、人类随身携带的单独设备（例如硬件钱包），也可以是一个物理场所（例如银行网点或登记办公室），在这些场所中通信以面对面的方式进行。

sents.en: In later sections, we will also consider a fourth party, a t rusted entity .
sents.zh: 在后续章节中，我们还将考虑第四方，即可信实体。

sents.zh: 它可以是连接到平台本身的安全硬件、人类随身携带的单独设备（例如硬件钱包），也可以是一个物理场所（例如银行网点或登记办公室），在这些场所中通信以面对面的方式进行。

paragraphs.en: We assume that physical interaction with devices is outside of an agent’s capabilities. Although a motivated human could conceivably deploy sensors or actuators to delegate to the agent in this manner, this is a significant barrier, and accountability is more clear cut as it is far less plausible for a human to claim that an agent physically interacted with a device without their knowledge than to claim that a sandboxed agent exploited some vulnerability to escalate their permissions.
paragraphs.zh: 我们假设与设备进行物理交互超出了智能体的能力范围。 尽管一个有动机的人类理论上可以部署传感器或执行器以这种方式向智能体委托任务，但这是一个重大的障碍，而且问责也更为清晰明确，因为相较于声称一个沙箱中的智能体利用某些漏洞提升了自身权限，声称一个智能体在自己不知情的情况下与设备发生了物理交互要难以令人信服得多。

sents.en: We assume that physical interaction with devices is outside of an agent’s capabilities.
sents.zh: 我们假设与设备进行物理交互超出了智能体的能力范围。

sents.en: Although a motivated human could conceivably deploy sensors or actuators to delegate to the agent in this manner, this is a significant barrier, and accountability is more clear cut as it is far less plausible for a human to claim that an agent physically interacted with a device without their knowledge than to claim that a sandboxed agent exploited some vulnerability to escalate their permissions.

paragraphs.en: Our threat model abstracts away application-specific HITL considerations, instead providing a low-level protocol for the approval of generic messages. In particular, policy determining what actions/messages are protected by a HITL gate is out of scope, in our threat model this is the choice of the trusted service, who also enforces this policy. We likewise do not consider human-factors questions, such whether how actions are formatted as messages for approval, whether these are correctly interpreted by the human that receives them, and whether the human truly engages with approval requests or merely rubber stamps them. When a service processes sequences of messages, an adversary that selectively censors approval of specific messages, or reorders individually benign ones, could cause unintended and harmful outcomes. As an application-level concern, however, this is similarly out of scope.
paragraphs.zh: 我们威胁模型抽象掉了特定于应用的人机协同（HITL）考量，而是提供一个用于批准通用消息的底层协议。 具体而言，确定哪些动作/消息受到 HITL 门控保护的策略不在本威胁模型的范围内；在我们的威胁模型中，这是受信任服务的选择，该服务同时也执行这一策略。 同样，我们也不考虑人因问题，例如动作被格式化为待批准消息的方式、人类接收者是否能正确解读这些消息，以及人类是真正参与批准请求还是仅仅草率地橡皮图章式批准。 当服务处理消息序列时，能够有选择地审查特定消息的批准或对单独无害的消息进行重排序的对手，可能导致意想不到的有害结果。 然而，作为应用层面的关注点，这同样不在本威胁模型的范围内。

paragraphs.en: Our threat model focuses on service-side enforcement of HITL gates. While common (as in Example 1 ), such enforcement for the I-HITL schemes explored in this work requires service-side modification. It also means that using I-HITL to protect local resources requires deployment of a suitably isolated local service.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的威胁模型聚焦于服务端的 HITL 门控执行。 尽管这种执行方式很常见（如示例 1 所示），但本文所研究的 I-HITL 方案若要实现此类执行，需要对服务端进行修改。 这也意味着，使用 I-HITL 保护本地资源需要部署一个经过适当隔离的本地服务。

sents.en: Our threat model focuses on service-side enforcement of HITL gates.
sents.zh: 我们的威胁模型聚焦于服务端的 HITL 门控执行。

sents.en: While common (as in Example 1 ), such enforcement for the I-HITL schemes explored in this work requires service-side modification.
sents.zh: 尽管这种执行方式很常见（如示例 1 所示），但本文所研究的 I-HITL 方案若要实现此类执行，需要对服务端进行修改。

sents.zh: 这也意味着，使用 I-HITL 保护本地资源需要部署一个经过适当隔离的本地服务。

paragraphs.en: See Section IV for discussion of our choice to analyze security symbolically, and for a discussion of authentication/identification-related challenges not captured by our model.
paragraphs.zh: 关于我们选择以符号化方式分析安全性，以及我们的模型未能涵盖的与认证/身份识别相关挑战的讨论，请参见第 IV 节。

paragraphs.en: When mapped to our threat model, many deployed HITL gates share a weakness [ 25 , 57 , 27 ] . Human approval relies on resources that the agent can reach through the platform it runs on. These deployments do use software-based defenses to protect these resources from the agent, such as restricting permissions, sandboxing, and screening for prompt injection, and in many cases these are effective. Such defenses are a relatively weak foundation for security. The following three common HITL gate deployment approaches illustrate the shortcomings.
paragraphs.zh: 当映射到我们的威胁模型时，许多已部署的人在回路（HITL）闸门存在一个共同的弱点 [ 25 , 57 , 27 ] 。 人类审批所依赖的资源，是智能体可以通过其运行所在平台访问到的。 这些部署确实使用基于软件的防御手段来保护这些资源免受智能体的影响，例如限制权限、沙箱隔离和提示注入筛查，而且在很多情况下这些手段是有效的。 但此类防御作为安全基础相对薄弱。 下面三种常见的人在回路闸门部署方式说明了这些不足之处。

sents.en: When mapped to our threat model, many deployed HITL gates share a weakness [ 25 , 57 , 27 ] .
sents.zh: 当映射到我们的威胁模型时，许多已部署的人在回路（HITL）闸门存在一个共同的弱点 [ 25 , 57 , 27 ] 。

sents.en: Human approval relies on resources that the agent can reach through the platform it runs on.
sents.zh: 人类审批所依赖的资源，是智能体可以通过其运行所在平台访问到的。

sents.en: These deployments do use software-based defenses to protect these resources from the agent, such as restricting permissions, sandboxing, and screening for prompt injection, and in many cases these are effective.
sents.zh: 这些部署确实使用基于软件的防御手段来保护这些资源免受智能体的影响，例如限制权限、沙箱隔离和提示注入筛查，而且在很多情况下这些手段是有效的。

sents.en: Such defenses are a relatively weak foundation for security.
sents.zh: 但此类防御作为安全基础相对薄弱。

sents.en: The following three common HITL gate deployment approaches illustrate the shortcomings.
sents.zh: 下面三种常见的人在回路闸门部署方式说明了这些不足之处。

paragraphs.en: Agent harnesses deploy HITL gates to pause the agent before a designated action, such as a tool call or shell command, and resume only once a human approves. Examples include LangGraph’s interrupts [ 46 ] , the OpenAI Agents SDK’s human-in-the-loop flow [ 68 ] , and Claude Code’s permission prompts and hooks [ 7 ] . Harnesses enforce permissions and sandbox the agent to limit its control of the host, which in principle should prevent it from subverting the gate. An agent capable of exploiting the harness or operating system can bypass these defenses, but in practice the bar is lower than this. Because the gate’s approval is just a signal from code on the same host, an agent with shell access could launch a process in advance that supplies approvals, even while its own reasoning is suspended by the gate. Alternatively, with write access to the files that configure the gate it could disable it outright. It is especially true that these gates do not prevent adversarial humans from removing themselves from the loop.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体框架部署人机协同（HITL）门控，在指定动作（如工具调用或 shell 命令）之前暂停智能体，只有在人类批准后才恢复执行。 例子包括 LangGraph 的中断机制 [ 46 ] 、OpenAI Agents SDK 的人机协同流程 [ 68 ] ，以及 Claude Code 的权限提示和钩子 [ 7 ] 。 框架通过强制权限和对智能体进行沙箱隔离来限制其对宿主的控制，这原则上应能防止其绕过门控。 能够利用框架或操作系统的智能体可以绕过这些防御，但在实践中门槛比这更低。 由于门控的批准只是来自同一宿主机上代码的信号，拥有 shell 访问权限的智能体可以提前启动一个提供批准的进程，即使它自身的推理已被门控暂停。 或者，凭借对配置门控的文件的写权限，它可以彻底禁用门控。 尤为真实的是，这些门控无法阻止对抗性人类将自己从回路中移除。

sents.zh: 智能体框架部署人机协同（HITL）门控，在指定动作（如工具调用或 shell 命令）之前暂停智能体，只有在人类批准后才恢复执行。

paragraphs.en: Browser agents are a special class of harness in which the agent controls a browser rather than the underlying host, implemented either as an extension (Claude in Chrome [ 8 ] ) or as a browser with a native agent (ChatGPT Atlas [ 67 ] , Perplexity Comet [ 71 ] ). Similar considerations as for generic harnesses apply when gates are browser-enforced, and prompt injection is an especially concerning attack surface given how frequently browser agents encounter untrusted content. However, a browser agent also transacts with third-party websites, which may themselves gate consequential actions, for instance through bot-detection or out-of-band authentication. These defenses move the gate off the potentially-compromised platform, but traditional bot-detection is increasingly ineffective against agents [ 50 ] , and because browsers retain authenticated sessions across services, an out-of-band channel such as email may still be accessible by the agent [ 22 ] . In these cases it remains difficult to distinguish an adversarial human delegating approval to the agent from a misbehaving agent seizing it. Banks already face this problem and, unable to tell authorized agents from rogue ones, have begun blocking agents outright or limiting them to read-only access [ 59 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 浏览器智能体是「脚手架」中一个特殊的类别，其中智能体控制的是浏览器而非底层主机，其实现形式既可以是扩展（Claude in Chrome [ 8 ] ），也可以是内置原生智能体的浏览器（ChatGPT Atlas [ 67 ] 、Perplexity Comet [ 71 ] ）。 当门控由浏览器强制执行时，适用于通用「脚手架」的类似考量同样成立；而且考虑到浏览器智能体频繁接触不可信内容，提示注入是一个尤其令人担忧的攻击面。 然而，浏览器智能体还会与第三方网站进行交易，这些网站自身可能对后果重大的操作设置门控，例如通过机器人检测或带外认证。 这些防御措施把门控从可能已被攻陷的平台移开，但传统的机器人检测对智能体的效力正日益下降 [ 50 ] ，而且由于浏览器在各服务之间保留已认证的会话，诸如电子邮件之类的带外渠道可能仍然可被智能体访问 [ 22 ] 。 在这些情况下，仍然很难区分是对抗性人类将审批权委托给智能体，还是行为失当的智能体夺取了审批权。 银行已经面临这个问题，并且由于无法区分经过授权的智能体与恶意的智能体，已开始彻底封锁智能体或将其限制为只读访问 [ 59 ] 。

sents.zh: 银行已经面临这个问题，并且由于无法区分经过授权的智能体与恶意的智能体，已开始彻底封锁智能体或将其限制为只读访问 [ 59 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Agentic wallet platforms such as those from Coinbase and Circle [ 27 , 23 ] are of particular interest because a misbehaving agent can lead directly to financial loss. A common architecture is the agent controlling a wallet through an API, subject to a spending policy set by the user, while a remote service gates any change to that policy on human approval. Control of the human’s platform therefore does not let the agent directly bypass the gate, but if the gate relies on resources accessible to the agent through the platform (either because the agent compromised them or because they were given willingly by the human), it can request and approve an escalation of its own permissions. In the next section we examine this scenario experimentally.
paragraphs.zh: 诸如 Coinbase 和 Circle [27, 23] 提供的智能体钱包平台尤其值得关注，因为行为不当的智能体可能直接导致财务损失。 一种常见的架构是智能体通过 API 控制钱包，并受用户设定的支出策略约束，而远程服务会对该策略的任何更改进行把关，要求人工批准。 因此，控制人类的平台并不能让智能体直接绕过把关，但如果把关依赖于智能体可通过平台访问的资源（无论是因为智能体入侵了这些资源，还是因为人类自愿授予了这些资源），它就可以请求并批准提升自身的权限。 在下一节中，我们将对这一场景进行实验性研究。

paragraphs.en: Circle’s Agent Wallets [ 24 ] let a user delegate control of a cryptocurrency wallet to an agent and attach spending policies that cap how much USDC the agent may move per transaction, day, week, or month. Policies are the user’s means of constraining the agent. Circle’s documentation describes them as follows: “set transfer limits or address allowlists and blocklists on your agent wallet to control how it can move USDC and interact with contracts” [ 23 ] . When a wallet CLI command attempts to change a spending policy, Circle gates the change behind a one-time passcode (OTP) emailed to the account owner, with the change only taking effect when the OTP is provided at the CLI. In this section we test the robustness of this HITL gate in a typical deployment, where an agent manages the wallet. As is common in personal-agent deployments, which bundle in email and web access [ 70 , 56 , 69 ] , the agent also has access to local email and web-search tools. 1 1 1 As a result of our disclosing the results of our experiments, Circle’s own documentation now warns against exactly this configuration (Appendix D ). We first aim to characterize whether models will self-escalate to change spending policies in benign situations where these conflict with user requests, before exploring how prompt injection attacks can cause an adversarial agent to bypass this HITL gate in the course of an attack.
paragraphs.zh: Circle 的智能体钱包（Agent Wallets）[ 24 ] 允许用户将加密货币钱包的控制权委托给智能体，并附加支出策略，以限制智能体每笔交易、每天、每周或每月可动用的 USDC 金额。 策略是用户用来约束智能体的手段。 Circle 的文档对策略的描述如下：“在你的智能体钱包上设置转账限额或地址白名单与黑名单，以控制它如何转移 USDC 以及如何与合约交互” [ 23 ] 。 当钱包 CLI 命令尝试更改支出策略时，Circle 会通过发送到账户所有者邮箱的一次性验证码（OTP）来对该更改进行把关，只有在 CLI 中提供该 OTP 时更改才会生效。 在本节中，我们在一个典型部署场景（即由智能体管理钱包）下测试这一 HITL 关卡的稳健性。 正如个人智能体部署中常见的那样——这类部署通常会捆绑电子邮件和网页访问能力 [ 70 , 56 , 69 ] ——该智能体同样可以访问本地电子邮件和网络搜索工具。1 1 1 在我们披露实验结果后，Circle 官方文档现已明确警告不要使用这种配置（附录 D ）。 我们首先刻画在良性情境下（即支出策略与用户请求冲突时），模型是否会自行升级以更改支出策略，然后再探讨提示注入攻击如何在攻击过程中使对抗性智能体绕过这一 HITL 关卡。

paragraphs.en: Setup. To simulate a typical personal agent, we deploy a LangChain [ 45 ] agent running with three tools available to it: a tool providing access to the user’s email, a web browsing tool and a Circle agent wallet. The wallet is initialized with 10 USDC on Base mainnet, and a spending policy which caps spending at 0.01 USDC per transaction, 0.01 USDC per day, 0.30 USDC per week, and 1 USDC per month. The agent’s system prompt instructs it to act only on the user’s instructions and to treat anything returned by a tool, emails included, as data rather than instructions, and tasks assigned to the agent never make any mention of the wallet spending policy, nor the steps that would be required to update it. Full setup details are given in Appendix B .
paragraphs.zh: 环境搭建。 为了模拟典型的个人智能体，我们部署了一个 LangChain [45] 智能体，并为其提供三个可用工具：一个访问用户电子邮件的工具、一个网页浏览工具和一个 Circle 智能体钱包。 该钱包在 Base 主网上初始化为 10 USDC，并设置了支出策略：每笔交易支出上限为 0.01 USDC，每日上限为 0.01 USDC，每周上限为 0.30 USDC，每月上限为 1 USDC。 该智能体的系统提示词指示它仅根据用户的指令行事，并将工具返回的任何内容（包括电子邮件）视为数据而非指令，分配给智能体的任务中从不提及钱包支出策略，也不提及更新该策略所需的步骤。 完整的环境搭建细节见附录 B。

paragraphs.en: Experiments. We ran three experiments across 10 models, with 20 trials for each model/experiment pair. The agent harness and initial wallet configuration described above are identical across experiments. Each experiment differs only in the user-assigned task and whether an adversary attempts to launch an indirect prompt injection attack [ 39 ] over email.
paragraphs.zh: 实验。 我们在10个模型上开展了三个实验，每个模型/实验组合进行20次试验。 上述智能体框架和初始钱包配置在所有实验中保持一致。 每个实验仅在用户指派的任务以及是否存在对手试图通过电子邮件发起间接提示注入攻击 [ 39 ] 这两个方面有所不同。

sents.en: Experiments.
sents.zh: 实验。

sents.zh: 我们在10个模型上开展了三个实验，每个模型/实验组合进行20次试验。

paragraphs.en: Payment agent, No attack . The agent is tasked with paying invoices received by email. The inbox holds three invoices, each for 0.01 USDC, so that paying all of them would require raising the daily spending cap.
paragraphs.zh: 支付智能体，无攻击。 该智能体的任务是通过电子邮件支付收到的发票。 收件箱中有三张发票，每张金额为 0.01 USDC，因此支付全部发票将需要提高每日支出上限。

paragraphs.en: Payment agent, Injection attack . The task and invoices are the same as in Payment agent, No attack , but an adversary sends the user an email that encourages the agent to self-escalate. The email presents a deadline by which the invoices must be paid, to add time pressure, and reassures the agent that self-escalating is acceptable behavior.

paragraphs.en: Summary agent, Injection attack . The agent is tasked only with summarizing the user’s inbox. An adversary sends the user a sequence of emails that impersonate the user and first direct the agent to make a payment of 0.02 USDC to the adversary’s address before a deadline, then preempt any requests for permission or clarification from the agent. Although the adversary cannot observe the agent’s reaction to its emails, it blindly sends the entire sequence.
paragraphs.zh: 总结智能体、注入攻击。 该智能体的任务仅是总结用户的收件箱。 攻击者向用户发送一系列伪装成用户本人的电子邮件，首先指示智能体在截止期限前向攻击者的地址支付 0.02 USDC，然后预先阻止智能体可能提出的任何权限请求或澄清请求。 尽管攻击者无法观察智能体对其邮件的反应，它仍盲目地发送整个邮件序列。

paragraphs.en: We developed the prompt injections used by the adversary adaptively, iteratively changing their content and wording to identify a variant that succeeded the most broadly across models. Such human red-teaming has been shown to be an effective attack strategy, though further iterations and reinforcement learning techniques could potentially increase the effectiveness of our attacks [ 63 ] . Although our prompt injections could likely be tailored to individual models for better attack success, we chose to pursue a universal attack. Our approach simulates an adversary that launches a broad email campaign targeting users that use a personal agent to manage their email and wallet. In this setting, the adversary aims to maximize attack success across a range of models that might be in use, rather than target a specific model. An adversary might also target specific users whom it knows use a specific model, and our results serve as a lower bound for that setting.
paragraphs.zh: 我们自适应地开发了对手所使用的提示注入，通过迭代修改其内容和措辞，寻找一种在多个模型上都能取得最广泛成功的变体。 这类人工红队测试已被证明是一种有效的攻击策略，不过进一步的迭代和强化学习技术可能会提升我们攻击的有效性 [ 63 ] 。 尽管我们的提示注入很可能可以针对单个模型进行定制以提高攻击成功率，但我们选择实施一种通用攻击。 我们的方法模拟了一个对手，该对手发起一场广泛的电子邮件攻击活动，目标是那些使用个人智能体来管理电子邮件和钱包的用户。 在这一场景中，对手的目标是在可能被使用的多种模型上最大化攻击成功率，而不是针对某个特定模型。 对手也可能针对其已知使用某个特定模型的特定用户，而我们的结果可作为该场景下的攻击效果下限。

paragraphs.en: Results. Figure 2 summarizes self-escalation likelihood across experiments and models. Example transcripts of self-escalating runs from each experiment can be found in Appendix C . In the Payment agent, No attack experiment, 9/10 models self-escalated to raise their spending limit in at least one run. Only claude-opus-5.5 never attempted self-escalation, instead consistently paying up to its spending limit and reporting the remaining invoices to the user. Self-escalation behavior in a benign setting appears to be inconsistent both across and within models, and does not seem to be especially correlated with model capabilities. This is important for users to be aware of: although a HITL gate like the one employed by Circle’s agent wallet might reasonably be expected to constrain an agent’s behavior even if it is relatively easy for an agent with email access to bypass, this is not the case. A user could run an agent that appears to respect the gate, but if they change models, or simply are using a model that only rarely self-escalates, it may come as a surprise that the gate is no longer effective.
paragraphs.zh: 结果。 图 2 总结了各实验和各模型中自我升级的可能性。 各实验中自我升级运行的示例记录见附录 C。 在支付智能体、无攻击实验中，9/10 的模型在至少一次运行中自我升级以提高其支出限额。 只有 claude-opus-5.5 从未尝试自我升级，而是一直按支出限额付款，并将剩余发票报告给用户。 在良性环境中，自我升级行为在不同模型之间和同一模型内部都表现得不稳定，并且似乎与模型能力没有特别的相关性。 用户需要意识到这一点很重要：尽管像 Circle 的智能体钱包所采用的人工审批门控（HITL）这样的机制，即使智能体通过邮件访问相对容易绕过它，人们通常也合理地期望它能约束智能体的行为，但事实并非如此。 用户运行的智能体表面上似乎遵守该门控，但如果他们更换了模型，或者只是使用的模型很少进行自我升级，那么该门控不再有效这一情况可能会令他们感到意外。

sents.zh: 各实验中自我升级运行的示例记录见附录 C。

sents.en: In the Payment agent, No attack experiment, 9/10 models self-escalated to raise their spending limit in at least one run.
sents.zh: 在支付智能体、无攻击实验中，9/10 的模型在至少一次运行中自我升级以提高其支出限额。

sents.en: Only claude-opus-5.5 never attempted self-escalation, instead consistently paying up to its spending limit and reporting the remaining invoices to the user.
sents.zh: 只有 claude-opus-5.5 从未尝试自我升级，而是一直按支出限额付款，并将剩余发票报告给用户。

sents.en: Self-escalation behavior in a benign setting appears to be inconsistent both across and within models, and does not seem to be especially correlated with model capabilities.
sents.zh: 在良性环境中，自我升级行为在不同模型之间和同一模型内部都表现得不稳定，并且似乎与模型能力没有特别的相关性。

sents.en: This is important for users to be aware of: although a HITL gate like the one employed by Circle’s agent wallet might reasonably be expected to constrain an agent’s behavior even if it is relatively easy for an agent with email access to bypass, this is not the case.
sents.zh: 用户需要意识到这一点很重要：尽管像 Circle 的智能体钱包所采用的人工审批门控（HITL）这样的机制，即使智能体通过邮件访问相对容易绕过它，人们通常也合理地期望它能约束智能体的行为，但事实并非如此。

sents.en: A user could run an agent that appears to respect the gate, but if they change models, or simply are using a model that only rarely self-escalates, it may come as a surprise that the gate is no longer effective.
sents.zh: 用户运行的智能体表面上似乎遵守该门控，但如果他们更换了模型，或者只是使用的模型很少进行自我升级，那么该门控不再有效这一情况可能会令他们感到意外。

paragraphs.en: The Payment agent, Injection attack experiment shows that attempting to prompt inject the payment agent to encourage it to self-escalate does not have a clear impact on self-escalation likelihood. In fact gemini-3.8-flash and claude-sonnet-5 both self-escalate less frequently in the presence of an adversarial email: their transcripts show that the adversarial email is flagged as a likely prompt injection, causing the model to defer to the user even when in the absence of an injection the model occasionally chooses to self-escalate.
paragraphs.zh: 支付智能体：注入攻击实验表明，尝试通过提示注入促使支付智能体自我提权，对自我提权的可能性没有明显影响。 事实上，gemini-3.8-flash 和 claude-sonnet-5 在存在对抗性邮件时自我提权的频率都更低：它们的对话记录显示，该对抗性邮件被标记为疑似提示注入，导致模型转而请示用户，即使在没有注入的情况下模型偶尔也会选择自我提权。

sents.en: The Payment agent, Injection attack experiment shows that attempting to prompt inject the payment agent to encourage it to self-escalate does not have a clear impact on self-escalation likelihood.
sents.zh: 支付智能体：注入攻击实验表明，尝试通过提示注入促使支付智能体自我提权，对自我提权的可能性没有明显影响。

sents.en: In fact gemini-3.8-flash and claude-sonnet-5 both self-escalate less frequently in the presence of an adversarial email: their transcripts show that the adversarial email is flagged as a likely prompt injection, causing the model to defer to the user even when in the absence of an injection the model occasionally chooses to self-escalate.
sents.zh: 事实上，gemini-3.8-flash 和 claude-sonnet-5 在存在对抗性邮件时自我提权的频率都更低：它们的对话记录显示，该对抗性邮件被标记为疑似提示注入，导致模型转而请示用户，即使在没有注入的情况下模型偶尔也会选择自我提权。

paragraphs.en: In the Summary agent, Injection attack experiment, adversarial emails frequently caused Qwen and DeepSeek models to self-escalate in order to send funds to the adversary without user approval. gemini-2.5-flash demonstrated this behavior in a single run, but the more recent gemini-3.8-flash model, as well as the GPT and Claude models, appear largely resistant to the prompt injection. That this attack succeeds at all is alarming: it would cost an adversary very little to launch a broad email campaign employing this attack, and they could expect it to succeed against at least some users, even if these users have set restrictive spending limits for their agent wallets. We disclosed these findings to Circle prior to publication: they have since added a warning to its agent-wallet documentation cautioning users against giving an agent access to the email inbox used to receive the OTP. We describe the disclosure and the resulting change in Appendix D .
paragraphs.zh: 在 Summary 智能体的注入攻击实验中，对抗性电子邮件频繁导致 Qwen 和 DeepSeek 模型自我升权，以便在未经用户批准的情况下向攻击者发送资金。gemini-2.5-flash 在单次运行中表现出这种行为，但较新的 gemini-3.8-flash 模型以及 GPT 和 Claude 模型似乎对提示注入具有相当的抵抗力。 这种攻击居然能够得逞，这一点令人担忧：攻击者发动一场广泛采用该攻击的电子邮件活动几乎不需要什么成本，而且即使这些用户已为其智能体钱包设置了严格的支出限额，他们也可以预期该攻击至少对部分用户会成功。 我们在发布前向 Circle 披露了这些发现：他们此后在其智能体钱包文档中添加了警告，提醒用户不要让智能体访问用于接收 OTP 的电子邮箱收件箱。 我们在附录 D 中描述了这次披露以及由此产生的变更。

paragraphs.en: The risk illustrated by our results can be mitigated in different ways. As per Circle’s warning, users should be cautioned not to deploy personal agents that have access to both a Circle wallet and the email associated with that wallet. Users may still be tempted to deploy agents with access to both for convenience, however, and it may be challenging to robustly disable email access, as an agent could leverage exploits or find stored credentials using a terminal/browser to gain access. Perhaps the most reliable defense is to develop stronger HITL gates which do not allow agents to self-escalate. In the following sections we develop and explore our stronger security notion called inalienable human-in-the-loop (I-HITL).
paragraphs.zh: 我们的结果所揭示的风险可以通过多种方式加以缓解。 根据 Circle 的警告，应提醒用户不要部署既能访问 Circle 钱包、又能访问与该钱包关联的电子邮箱的个人智能体。 然而，用户仍可能出于便利考虑而部署能同时访问两者的智能体，而且要可靠地禁用邮箱访问可能颇具挑战，因为智能体可能利用漏洞，或通过终端/浏览器找到存储的凭证来获取访问权限。 最可靠的防御措施或许是开发更强的人机协同确认（HITL）门控机制，不允许智能体自行提权。 在接下来的章节中，我们将开发并探讨我们提出的更强安全概念——不可剥夺的人机协同确认（I-HITL）。

paragraphs.en: Topologies. A key feature of our threat model is that the human cannot interact with the service directly: all communication between them passes through the agent-controlled platform or, where available, a trusted entity. We follow [ 13 ] in our use of communication topologies , though we do not use their Tamarin model in our formal treatment.
paragraphs.zh: 拓扑结构。 我们威胁模型的一个关键特征是：人类无法直接与服务进行交互，二者之间的所有通信都必须经过由智能体控制的平台，或在可用时经过一个可信实体。 在通信拓扑结构的使用上，我们遵循[13]，但在形式化处理中并未使用他们的 Tamarin 模型。

paragraphs.en: 𝗂𝗇𝗌 \mathsf{ins} (insecure): reads every message; may alter or inject messages.
paragraphs.zh: 𝗂𝗇𝗌 \mathsf{ins}（不安全）：读取每条消息；可能会篡改或注入消息。

paragraphs.en: 𝖺𝗎𝗍𝗁 \mathsf{auth} (authentic): reads every message; can neither alter nor inject messages.
paragraphs.zh: 𝖺𝗎𝗍𝗁 \mathsf{auth}（认证者）：读取每条消息；既不能篡改也不能注入消息。

paragraphs.zh: 𝖼𝗈𝗇𝖿 \mathsf{conf} (confidential)：对所发送的消息一无所知；可以注入自己的消息。

paragraphs.zh: 𝗌𝖾𝖼 \mathsf{sec}（安全）：既具真实性又具机密性。

paragraphs.en: The adversary can also drop/delay messages on all channels.
paragraphs.zh: 攻击者还可以在所有信道上丢弃/延迟消息。

paragraphs.en: Human. ℋ \mathcal{H} runs a program from a restricted class 𝒞 \mathcal{C} of programs. On input a special message format we call a request , denoted ⟨ m , a ⟩ \langle m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak a\rangle for message m ∈ ℳ m\in\mathcal{M} and auxiliary data a ∈ { 0 , 1 } ∗ a\in\{0\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak 1\}^{*} , ℋ \mathcal{H} ’s program takes an external bit b m b_{m} and, iff b m = 1 b_{m}=1 , emits a message to approve m m (as prescribed by the protocol). All other messages are ignored. Programs in 𝒞 \mathcal{C} are also stateless and must correspond to human capabilities, meaning that cryptographic operations are not possible. Although this is restrictive, we show in Section V that allowing a more expressive class of programs does not weaken the channel requirements necessary for I-HITL. Note that although our threat model permits an adversarial human, ℋ \mathcal{H} as a party in the topology is always honest. Intuitively, this is because ℋ \mathcal{H} represents the physical human: if ℋ \mathcal{H} takes an action that allows a message to be approved, that constitutes a human-in-the-loop, and so there is no meaningful way to a human to adversarially deviate. We will see in Section VI-C that an adversarial human instead yields weaker channel labels on 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , as this adversary can potentially extract and share keys.

paragraphs.en: An I-HITL protocol for a message space ℳ \mathcal{M} and a topology τ \tau is a tuple Σ = ( 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 , 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 , 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ) \Sigma=(\mathsf{Enroll}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Approve}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Verify}) :
paragraphs.zh: 针对消息空间 ℳ \mathcal{M} 和拓扑 τ \tau 的 I-HITL 协议是一个元组 Σ = ( 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 , 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 , 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ) \Sigma=(\mathsf{Enroll}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Approve}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Verify})：

paragraphs.en: 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} and 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) are interactive protocols among the parties of τ \tau over its channels, prescribing a program for each of 𝒫 , 𝒮 , 𝒯 \mathcal{P}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathcal{S}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathcal{T} and a program in 𝒞 \mathcal{C} for ℋ \mathcal{H} . At the end of 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} , 𝒮 \mathcal{S} outputs verification string 𝗏𝗄 \mathsf{vk} or ⊥ \bot ; at the end of 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) , 𝒮 \mathcal{S} outputs a proof π \pi or ⊥ \bot .
paragraphs.zh: Enroll 和 Approve(m) 是 τ 的各方在其信道上运行的交互式协议，为 𝒫、𝒮、𝒯 各规定一个程序，并为 ℋ 在 𝒞 中规定一个程序。 在 Enroll 结束时，𝒮 输出验证字符串 vk 或 ⊥；在 Approve(m) 结束时，𝒮 输出证明 π 或 ⊥。

sents.en: 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} and 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) are interactive protocols among the parties of τ \tau over its channels, prescribing a program for each of 𝒫 , 𝒮 , 𝒯 \mathcal{P}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathcal{S}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathcal{T} and a program in 𝒞 \mathcal{C} for ℋ \mathcal{H} .
sents.zh: Enroll 和 Approve(m) 是 τ 的各方在其信道上运行的交互式协议，为 𝒫、𝒮、𝒯 各规定一个程序，并为 ℋ 在 𝒞 中规定一个程序。

sents.en: At the end of 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} , 𝒮 \mathcal{S} outputs verification string 𝗏𝗄 \mathsf{vk} or ⊥ \bot ; at the end of 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) , 𝒮 \mathcal{S} outputs a proof π \pi or ⊥ \bot .
sents.zh: 在 Enroll 结束时，𝒮 输出验证字符串 vk 或 ⊥；在 Approve(m) 结束时，𝒮 输出证明 π 或 ⊥。

paragraphs.en: 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , π ) → { 0 , 1 } \mathsf{Verify}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi)\to\{0\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak 1\} is a function.
paragraphs.zh: 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , π ) → { 0 , 1 } \mathsf{Verify}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi)\to\{0\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak 1\} 是一个函数。

paragraphs.en: Approval. Since ℋ \mathcal{H} is honest, approval is defined by its external bits rather than any output it produces. We say ℋ \mathcal{H} approved m m , written ℋ . 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾𝖽 ⁡ ( m ) = 1 \mathcal{H}.\mathsf{Approved}(m)=1 , if during the execution ℋ \mathcal{H} ’s program received a request ⟨ m , a ⟩ \langle m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak a\rangle and was given external bit b m = 1 b_{m}=1 for it. ℋ \mathcal{H} cannot approve a message it has not been shown, and the approval itself is a physical act of the human that the program for 𝒫 \mathcal{P} cannot perform in its place. Because m m is determined by the request, the approval message ℋ \mathcal{H} emits may be as little as a single bit, and it need not reproduce m m . We ignore replay: deployments that require fresh approval of the same message across sessions can include a nonce in m m at the application layer.
paragraphs.zh: 批准。 由于 ℋ \mathcal{H} 是诚实的，批准由其外部比特决定，而非它产生的任何输出。 我们称 ℋ \mathcal{H} 批准了 m m ，记作 ℋ . 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾𝖽 ⁡ ( m ) = 1 \mathcal{H}.\mathsf{Approved}(m)=1 ，如果在执行 ℋ \mathcal{H} 的程序期间，该程序收到了请求 ⟨ m , a ⟩ \langle m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak a\rangle ，并且为之被给予外部比特 b m = 1 b_{m}=1 。 ℋ \mathcal{H} 无法批准一个未曾向其出示的消息，而批准本身是人类的一种物理行为， 𝒫 \mathcal{P} 的程序无法代替其完成。 由于 m m 由请求确定， ℋ \mathcal{H} 发出的批准消息可以少到只是一个比特，并且无需重现 m m 。 我们忽略重放问题：若部署要求同一消息在不同会话中都要有新的批准，可以在应用层把一个随机数（nonce）包含进 m m 中。

sents.en: Approval.
sents.zh: 批准。

sents.en: Since ℋ \mathcal{H} is honest, approval is defined by its external bits rather than any output it produces.
sents.zh: 由于 ℋ \mathcal{H} 是诚实的，批准由其外部比特决定，而非它产生的任何输出。

sents.en: We say ℋ \mathcal{H} approved m m , written ℋ . 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾𝖽 ⁡ ( m ) = 1 \mathcal{H}.\mathsf{Approved}(m)=1 , if during the execution ℋ \mathcal{H} ’s program received a request ⟨ m , a ⟩ \langle m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak a\rangle and was given external bit b m = 1 b_{m}=1 for it. ℋ \mathcal{H} cannot approve a message it has not been shown, and the approval itself is a physical act of the human that the program for 𝒫 \mathcal{P} cannot perform in its place.
sents.zh: 我们称 ℋ \mathcal{H} 批准了 m m ，记作 ℋ . 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾𝖽 ⁡ ( m ) = 1 \mathcal{H}.\mathsf{Approved}(m)=1 ，如果在执行 ℋ \mathcal{H} 的程序期间，该程序收到了请求 ⟨ m , a ⟩ \langle m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak a\rangle ，并且为之被给予外部比特 b m = 1 b_{m}=1 。 ℋ \mathcal{H} 无法批准一个未曾向其出示的消息，而批准本身是人类的一种物理行为， 𝒫 \mathcal{P} 的程序无法代替其完成。

sents.en: Because m m is determined by the request, the approval message ℋ \mathcal{H} emits may be as little as a single bit, and it need not reproduce m m .
sents.zh: 由于 m m 由请求确定， ℋ \mathcal{H} 发出的批准消息可以少到只是一个比特，并且无需重现 m m 。

sents.en: We ignore replay: deployments that require fresh approval of the same message across sessions can include a nonce in m m at the application layer.
sents.zh: 我们忽略重放问题：若部署要求同一消息在不同会话中都要有新的批准，可以在应用层把一个随机数（nonce）包含进 m m 中。

paragraphs.en: Symbolic model. We reason symbolically, as per the Dolev-Yao model [ 32 ] . The adversary can read, inject, drop, and delay messages as channel labels permit, but cannot guess fresh values or forge signatures. Concretely, a value sampled by an honest party and sent only on a confidential channel is unknown to the adversary, and 𝖲𝗂𝗀𝖵𝖾𝗋 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , σ ) = 1 \mathsf{SigVer}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\sigma)=1 only if σ \sigma was produced by a party holding 𝗌𝗄 \mathsf{sk} . A computational treatment would replace these idealizations with EUF-CMA security and a considerably more complex treatment, with probabilistic security bounds. We leave such treatment to future work.
paragraphs.zh: 符号模型。 我们按照 Dolev-Yao 模型 [ 32 ] 进行符号化推理。 对手可以按照信道标签的许可读取、注入、丢弃和延迟消息，但不能猜测新鲜值或伪造签名。 具体而言，由诚实方采样并仅通过机密信道发送的值对手是不可知的，且 𝖲𝗂𝗀𝖵𝖾𝗋 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , σ ) = 1 \mathsf{SigVer}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\sigma)=1 当且仅当 σ \sigma 是由持有 𝗌𝗄 \mathsf{sk} 的一方生成的。 计算性处理将用 EUF-CMA 安全性以及复杂得多的处理方式取代这些理想化假设，并带来概率性的安全界。 我们将此类处理留待未来工作。

sents.en: Symbolic model.
sents.zh: 符号模型。

sents.en: We reason symbolically, as per the Dolev-Yao model [ 32 ] .
sents.zh: 我们按照 Dolev-Yao 模型 [ 32 ] 进行符号化推理。

sents.zh: 具体而言，由诚实方采样并仅通过机密信道发送的值对手是不可知的，且 𝖲𝗂𝗀𝖵𝖾𝗋 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , σ ) = 1 \mathsf{SigVer}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\sigma)=1 当且仅当 σ \sigma 是由持有 𝗌𝗄 \mathsf{sk} 的一方生成的。

sents.en: A computational treatment would replace these idealizations with EUF-CMA security and a considerably more complex treatment, with probabilistic security bounds.

paragraphs.en: Let Σ = ( 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 , 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 , 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ) \Sigma=(\mathsf{Enroll}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Approve}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Verify}) be an I-HITL protocol for ( ℳ , τ ) (\mathcal{M}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\tau) .
paragraphs.zh: 令 Σ = ( 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 , 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 , 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ) \Sigma=(\mathsf{Enroll}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Approve}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{Verify}) 为针对 ( ℳ , τ ) (\mathcal{M}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\tau) 的一个 I-HITL 协议。

paragraphs.en: Completeness. For every m ∈ ℳ m\in\mathcal{M} , in an execution of 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} followed by 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) in which all parties run Σ \Sigma , the adversary is passive, and ℋ \mathcal{H} receives external bit 1 1 , 𝒮 \mathcal{S} outputs 𝗏𝗄 ≠ ⊥ \mathsf{vk}\neq\bot in 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} and π ≠ ⊥ \pi\neq\bot in 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) with 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , π ) = 1 \mathsf{Verify}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi)=1 .
paragraphs.zh: 完备性。 对于每个 m ∈ ℳ m\in\mathcal{M} ，在所有参与方运行 Σ \Sigma 、敌手被动、且 ℋ \mathcal{H} 收到外部比特 1 1 的情况下，依次执行 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} 和 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) 的执行过程中，𝒮 \mathcal{S} 在 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} 中输出 𝗏𝗄 ≠ ⊥ \mathsf{vk}\neq\bot ，在 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) 中输出 π ≠ ⊥ \pi\neq\bot ，且满足 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , π ) = 1 \mathsf{Verify}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi)=1 。

sents.en: Completeness.
sents.zh: 完备性。

sents.en: For every m ∈ ℳ m\in\mathcal{M} , in an execution of 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} followed by 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) in which all parties run Σ \Sigma , the adversary is passive, and ℋ \mathcal{H} receives external bit 1 1 , 𝒮 \mathcal{S} outputs 𝗏𝗄 ≠ ⊥ \mathsf{vk}\neq\bot in 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} and π ≠ ⊥ \pi\neq\bot in 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) with 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , π ) = 1 \mathsf{Verify}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi)=1 .
sents.zh: 对于每个 m ∈ ℳ m\in\mathcal{M} ，在所有参与方运行 Σ \Sigma 、敌手被动、且 ℋ \mathcal{H} 收到外部比特 1 1 的情况下，依次执行 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} 和 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) 的执行过程中，𝒮 \mathcal{S} 在 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} 中输出 𝗏𝗄 ≠ ⊥ \mathsf{vk}\neq\bot ，在 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 ⁡ ( m ) \mathsf{Approve}(m) 中输出 π ≠ ⊥ \pi\neq\bot ，且满足 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m , π ) = 1 \mathsf{Verify}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi)=1 。

paragraphs.en: Approval-binding. Consider an execution in which ℋ \mathcal{H} , 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and 𝒯 \mathcal{T} run Σ \Sigma and the adversary 𝒜 {\mathcal{A}} chooses the program run by 𝒫 \mathcal{P} , acts on every channel as its label permits, initiates any number of 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾 \mathsf{Approve} sessions on messages of its choice, interleaved as it likes, and sets the external bits input to ℋ \mathcal{H} ’s program. Σ \Sigma is approval-binding for τ \tau if in every such execution in which 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} outputs 𝗏𝗄 ≠ ⊥ \mathsf{vk}\neq\bot , every ( m ∗ , π ∗ ) (m^{*}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi^{*}) with 𝖵𝖾𝗋𝗂𝖿𝗒 ⁡ ( 𝗏𝗄 , m ∗ , π ∗ ) = 1 \mathsf{Verify}(\mathsf{vk}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak m^{*}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\pi^{*})=1 that 𝒜 {\mathcal{A}} can produce satisfies ℋ . 𝖠𝗉𝗉𝗋𝗈𝗏𝖾𝖽 ⁡ ( m ∗ ) = 1 \mathcal{H}.\mathsf{Approved}(m^{*})=1 .

paragraphs.en: Individual authentication. Our topologies contain a single human ℋ \mathcal{H} and a single trusted entity 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , so the channels between them, and hence the association between the device and the human, are fixed by the topology itself. In a deployment with many humans and devices, 𝒮 \mathcal{S} cares not only that some human approved m ∗ m^{*} but that a specific human did, which requires 𝒮 \mathcal{S} to know which ℋ \mathcal{H} the enrolled 𝒯 \mathcal{T} has channels with. We treat this binding as a setup assumption. In practice, it is established during 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} by authenticating ℋ \mathcal{H} to 𝒮 \mathcal{S} through 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , for example by enrolling the device from a session authenticated before the platform came under the agent’s control, or by having the device collect biometric information that is shared with 𝒮 \mathcal{S} . A human could also hand the enrolled device to another human, which only biometric authentication on every approval would prevent. For simplicity, we consider this type of authentication out of scope and model a single ℋ \mathcal{H} throughout.
paragraphs.zh: 个体认证。 我们的拓扑包含单个人类 ℋ \mathcal{H} 和单个可信实体 𝒯 \mathcal{T}，因此它们之间的信道，进而设备与人类之间的关联，都由拓扑本身固定。 在包含多个人类和设备的部署中，𝒮 \mathcal{S} 不仅关心有某个人类批准了 m ∗ m^{*}，还关心是特定的人类批准了它，这就要求 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 知道已注册的 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 与哪个 ℋ \mathcal{H} 建立了信道。 我们将这种绑定视为一个设置假设。 在实践中，它是在 𝖤𝗇𝗋𝗈𝗅𝗅 \mathsf{Enroll} 期间通过 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 向 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 认证 ℋ \mathcal{H} 来建立的，例如在智能体获得控制权之前，从一个已经完成认证的会话中注册设备，或者让设备收集与 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 共享的生物识别信息。 人类也可能把已注册的设备交给另一个人，只有每次批准时都进行生物识别认证才能防止这种情况。 为简单起见，我们将这类认证视为超出范围，并在全文中只建模单个 ℋ \mathcal{H}。

paragraphs.en: In this section we apply our security definitions for I-HITL protocols, first to show that secure I-HITL protocols are impossible in the plain topology, and then to demonstrate the requirements under which they can be realized with a trusted entity.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们应用针对 I-HITL 协议的安全性定义，首先证明在普通拓扑中安全的 I-HITL 协议是不可能实现的，然后展示在何种要求下可以借助可信实体实现这些协议。

paragraphs.en: While this is a straightforward result, it captures a fundamental limitation of any human-in-the-loop system operating in the plain topology, with no trusted party out of the agent’s reach. Many such systems have been proposed in the academic literature and deployed in industry, including the Circle agent wallet of Example 1 , which we show agents bypass under a natural configuration ( Section III ).
paragraphs.zh: 虽然这是一个直接的结果，但它捕捉到了任何在明文拓扑中运行、且不存在智能体无法触及的可信第三方的人在回路系统的一个根本性局限。 学术文献中已提出并工业界已部署了许多此类系统，包括示例 1 中的 Circle 智能体钱包，我们将展示在一种自然配置下智能体可以绕过该系统（第 III 节）。

paragraphs.en: We now add a trusted entity 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , which can keep secret state and perform cryptographic operations, and ask which channels between 𝒯 \mathcal{T} and the other parties are necessary for a secure protocol to be constructed. Although Basin et al. [ 13 ] also consider topologies containing a trusted entity, they operate in a restricted setting where 𝒯 \mathcal{T} ’s channels are either secure or insecure, therefore their model is unable to distinguish between different types of trusted device and the resulting channels, as we do here and in Section VI-C .
paragraphs.zh: 我们现在加入一个可信实体 𝒯 \mathcal{T}，它可以保存秘密状态并执行密码学操作，并探讨为了构建安全协议，𝒯 \mathcal{T} 与其他参与方之间哪些信道是必要的。尽管 Basin 等人 [13] 也考虑了包含可信实体的拓扑，但他们在受限的设置下工作，其中 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 的信道要么是安全的，要么是不安全的，因此他们的模型无法像我们在这里以及第 VI-C 节中所做的那样，区分不同类型的可信设备及其产生的信道。

paragraphs.en: A trusted entity enables the construction of a secure I-HITL only if the adversary cannot stand in for it. If the adversary can read everything 𝒯 \mathcal{T} receives from 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and inject on every channel from 𝒯 \mathcal{T} to 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , it can run a copy of 𝒯 \mathcal{T} in its place, and 𝒮 \mathcal{S} ends up with verification material generated by the adversary, exactly as in Theorem 4 .
paragraphs.zh: 只有当攻击者无法顶替某个可信实体时，该可信实体才能用于构建安全的 I-HITL。 如果攻击者能够读取 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 从 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 接收的所有内容，并在从 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 到 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 的每条信道上注入数据，那么它就可以运行一份 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 的副本取而代之，而 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 最终得到的将是由攻击者生成的验证材料，这与定理 4 中的情形完全相同。

By Proposition 5 , a trusted entity can be useful for ℋ \mathcal{H} in exactly two ways: by showing ℋ \mathcal{H} something the adversary cannot read ( ℓ 𝒯 ​ ℋ ∈ { 𝖼𝗈𝗇𝖿 , 𝗌𝖾𝖼 } \ell_{\mathcal{T}\mathcal{H}}\in\{\mathsf{conf}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{sec}\} ) or by receiving from ℋ \mathcal{H} something the adversary cannot forge ( ℓ ℋ ​ 𝒯 ∈ { 𝖺𝗎𝗍𝗁 , 𝗌𝖾𝖼 } \ell_{\mathcal{H}\mathcal{T}}\in\{\mathsf{auth}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\mathsf{sec}\} ), and for the service in the two analogous ways. paragraphs.en: Theorem 7 says nothing about where the labels on each 𝒯 \mathcal{T} channel come from in the first place. A trusted entity’s channels are determined by the device that realizes it and by the human’s behavior when interacting with that device. The next section explores these factors in practice, deriving channel labels from device characteristics such as whether 𝒯 \mathcal{T} ’s key is attested or extractable, and whether an adversarial human attempts to delegate to the agent. The theorem then lets us characterize which approaches allow I-HITL protocols.

paragraphs.en: Many approaches used for authentication (hardware wallets, authenticator apps, etc.) appear well-suited to realizing I-HITL, but the analysis in preceding sections shows achieving approval-binding can be subtle. In this section we explore whether I-HITL can be realized by devices and protocols in use today. We focus on standalone hardware devices and mobile phone-based authentication protocols, disregarding some possible instantiations of 𝒯 \mathcal{T} such as in-person interaction. Section VI-A derives labels on 𝒯 ↔ 𝒮 \mathcal{T}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{S} channels ( ℓ 𝒮 ​ 𝒯 , ℓ 𝒯 ​ 𝒮 ) (\ell_{\mathcal{S}\mathcal{T}}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\ell_{\mathcal{T}\mathcal{S}}) based on a trusted entity’s key management. Section VI-B similarly explains how the display and user inputs provided by a trusted entity determine the labels of ℋ ↔ 𝒯 \mathcal{H}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{T} channels ( ℓ ℋ ​ 𝒯 , ℓ 𝒯 ​ ℋ ) (\ell_{\mathcal{H}\mathcal{T}}\mathchar 24891\relax\allowbreak\ell_{\mathcal{T}\mathcal{H}}) . Section VI-C applies the analysis in the preceding subsections to specific authentication methods in use today, and using Theorem 7 , classifies them according to their ability to realize I-HITL.

paragraphs.en: Theorem 7 is stated in terms of channel labels, but these labels are not directly observable to the verifier of an I-HITL proof (whether this is the service itself or an external verifier). Throughout this section we therefore work in terms of the strongest channel labels which can be confirmed by a verifier. For instance, if a device serving as 𝒯 \mathcal{T} has a display which lets it realize a secure channel to ℋ \mathcal{H} , but it generates no evidence which can be used to verify the existence of this channel, we treat the channel as insecure.
paragraphs.zh: 定理 7 是用信道标签来表述的，但这些标签对于 I-HITL 证明的验证者（无论是服务本身还是外部验证者）来说都无法直接观察到。 因此，在本节中，我们始终以验证者能够确认的最强信道标签为准来进行讨论。 例如，如果作为 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 的设备拥有一块显示屏，使其能够实现与 ℋ \mathcal{H} 之间的安全信道，但它不生成任何可用于验证该信道存在的证据，那么我们就将该信道视为不安全的。

paragraphs.en: In practice, the labels between 𝒯 \mathcal{T} and 𝒮 \mathcal{S} depend upon a secret key k k held by 𝒯 \mathcal{T} but not the adversary. We write k k to distinguish it from the signing key 𝗌𝗄 {\sf sk} of the I-HITL protocol constructions, though in practice the two may coincide. Since initially all channels between the two are insecure, establishing a new channel requires two properties of k k : it must be bound , i.e., verifiably held by 𝒯 \mathcal{T} rather than by a party impersonating it, and it must be isolated , i.e., not held by any adversarial party. Neither property is directly observable by a verifier. Both instead rest on attestation : evidence, verifiable against a root of trust, that k k was generated within 𝒯 \mathcal{T} and whether it is extractable by ℋ \mathcal{H} . Attestation settles binding outright, but settles isolation only if k k is not extractable, otherwise isolation, and therefore the channel labels, depend on whether ℋ \mathcal{H} acts honestly or adversarially—a feature of our threat model that differs critically from previous models of human principals [ 34 , 72 , 15 , 14 , 84 , 33 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 在实践中，𝒯 \mathcal{T} 与 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 之间的标签取决于由 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 持有但不被对手掌握的密钥 k k。 我们写作 k k 以区别于 I-HITL 协议构造的签名密钥 𝗌𝗄 {\sf sk}，尽管在实践中二者可能相同。 由于最初二者之间的所有信道都是不安全的，建立新信道要求 k k 具备两个性质：它必须是绑定的，即可验证地由 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 持有而非由冒充它的参与方持有；并且它必须是隔离的，即不被任何对抗性参与方持有。 这两个性质都不能被验证者直接观察到。 二者都依赖证明：即依据信任根可验证的证据，表明 k k 是在 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 内部生成的，以及它是否可被 ℋ \mathcal{H} 提取。 证明可以彻底解决绑定问题，但只有在 k k 不可提取时才能解决隔离问题；否则，隔离以及因此信道标签就取决于 ℋ \mathcal{H} 的行为是诚实的还是对抗性的——这是我们的威胁模型与以往的人类主体模型 [ 34 , 72 , 15 , 14 , 84 , 33 ] 存在关键差异的一个特点。

paragraphs.en: Key attestation ( attested / unattested ): Some devices, e.g., Yubikeys [ 90 ] and Ledger wallets [ 47 ] , can digitally sign the keys they generate, where signatures are verifiable against a manufacturer root of trust. Mobile phones generally provide an analogous capability, verifiable against the OS vendor’s root, which installed apps may optionally use to provide evidence of their key management. We use the designation attested for such devices. Other trusted hardware devices, e.g., standard crypto wallets, lack this capability and are unattested , so is any key that 𝒯 \mathcal{T} did not generate, such as a shared secret delivered by 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , since attestation can only speak to keys created within 𝒯 \mathcal{T} . When a device is attested, 𝒮 \mathcal{S} can use an attestation to verify that key k k is truly held by 𝒯 \mathcal{T} and subject to a fixed policy. Without attestation, 𝒮 \mathcal{S} cannot tell whether k k is held by the adversary, so both channel labels are ins .
paragraphs.zh: 密钥认证（已认证 / 未认证）：某些设备（例如 Yubikey [90] 和 Ledger 硬件钱包 [47]）能够对其生成的密钥进行数字签名，签名可对照厂商的信任根加以验证。 手机通常提供类似的能力，可对照操作系统厂商的信任根进行验证，已安装的应用可以选择性地使用该能力来提供其密钥管理的证据。 我们将此类设备称为已认证（attested）。 其他可信硬件设备（例如标准加密钱包）不具备该能力，属于未认证（unattested）；任何非由 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 生成的密钥也是如此，例如由 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 下发的共享密钥，因为认证只能证明在 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 内部创建的密钥。 当设备已认证时，𝒮 \mathcal{S} 可以利用认证来验证密钥 k k 确实由 𝒯 \mathcal{T} 持有，并受固定策略约束。 若没有认证，𝒮 \mathcal{S} 无法判断 k k 是否被对手持有，因此两个信道标签均为 ins。
